payload.name: Extract Detailed Past Events with Time Anchors
payload.description: When a user narrates a specific past experience with a time anchor such as 'last week' or 'yesterday', during extraction create an event memory for that occurrence, even if the message also expresses feelings or preferences.
content: During extraction, if a message narrates a concrete past event the speaker experienced (e.g., an outing, sighting, visit, or occurrence) and includes a relative or absolute time anchor, create a separate event memory capturing the activity, key details, and timing resolved from the message/session timestamp; do not fold it only into a preference, state, or comfort-source memory.
If the same message also contains emotional or supportive content, still emit the event candidate separately from any comfort/joy source memory.
Record only explicitly stated factual details; do not infer unmentioned participants, places, or outcomes. Emit at most one event per distinct occurrence and stop once the event is captured.

solves: This solves the failure to persist concrete past events that users mention in casual conversation, especially when those messages also contain emotional or preference language. Without this rule, such events are omitted because the extractor focuses on feelings or other memory types, leaving future questions about what/when unanswered.
